abstract: This article investigates AI 'slop' creators in China who use generative AI tools to systematically produce viral short videos on platforms. It argues that these creators transform virality from an unpredictable outcome into an object of deliberate, managed production through practices such as benchmarking viral content, testing formats, and operating matrix account systems. The study reframes emerging AI-assisted creative labour and challenges conventional understandings of what it means to be a 'creator' in platform-based cultural production.
key_claims: Generative AI is producing new forms of creative labour that challenge established notions of the 'creator'.
AI slop creators in China treat virality as an object of systematic management rather than an unpredictable outcome.
The formalisation and industrialisation of viral content production reshapes cultural production on platforms.
methods: Ethnographic approach studying AI slop creators in China (details truncated in the available abstract).
findings: Creators benchmark viral content and test formats to reverse-engineer what succeeds.
Creators operate matrix account systems and formalise production workflows.
These practices convert virality into a managed, engineered outcome.
contributions: Introduces and analyses 'AI slop' creators as a distinct category of platform-based creative labour.
Offers empirical insight into AI-assisted viral video production within the Chinese platform context.
Advances theoretical understanding of creativity and labour in generative-AI-driven cultural production.
framing: The paper situates itself within scholarship on platform-based cultural production, creative labour, and generative AI, interrogating how AI-embedded workflows unsettle established definitions of the 'creator'.
